answer: The inlet enters each head it grants into the nebula it keeps for that maker, and the tally rides on coin, so a purse fed from counted coin inherits it. Each new head must be carried in by falcons who have never carried for this maker, one more falcon than the nebula already holds heads, and every falcon is paid a coin, locked at the inlet, forfeit if that head is judged a twin. The first head costs one falcon and one coin; a maker's thousandth needs a thousand fresh falcons, five hundred thousand five hundred in all, none of them spendable twice.
